# v6blick

> v6blick is a command-line tool, written in Rust, that tests whether a website works for someone who has no IPv4. Phase 0 works: `check` and `doctor`, ten checks, text and JSON output. There are no ready-built binaries yet; build it with `cargo install --git https://github.com/cschweda/v6blick` (tag `v0.1.0`, Rust 1.88 or later). It needs working IPv6 on the machine it runs on; GitHub's hosted runners have none by default.

Today v6blick connects to a host over IPv4 and over IPv6 separately and compares the two. Planned: load a whole page from three kinds of network, `dual` (an ordinary connection), `nat64` (IPv6-only with a NAT64 translator, simulated) and `v6only` (IPv6-only with no translator), and report what breaks in each. Findings have stable check IDs, four severities (critical, warning, notice, info), a plain statement with every finding of what it means and how to fix it, JSON output and exit codes for CI (0 clean, 1 notices or warnings, 2 critical, 3 the run failed).

## Commands

- `v6blick check <host-or-url>`: DNS and connection checks over IPv4 and IPv6 separately, and a comparison of the two. No browser. Works today.
- `v6blick doctor`: whether this machine has working IPv6 and whether Chrome or Chromium is installed. Works today.
- `v6blick page <url>`: loads the page in an installed Chrome through a local proxy that enforces each network mode, and lists every resource that fails. Planned.

## Checks

- ADR-01 to ADR-03: addresses (no AAAA record, an unusable AAAA record, a zone that cannot be resolved over IPv6 alone)
- RCH-01 to RCH-04: reachability (a published AAAA that nothing answers, TLS failing over IPv6 only, slow IPv6 connects, a long wait before IPv4 takes over)
- EQV-01 to EQV-03: equivalence (a different certificate, status, redirect or body over IPv6)
- PGE-01 to PGE-04: page resources that fail without IPv4 (planned, needs a browser)
- LIT-01 to LIT-02: literal IPv4 addresses in a page (planned, needs a browser)
- MTU-01: large responses that stall over IPv6 only (planned)

## Security

One red team and blue team audit so far, of version 0.1.0 on 2026-11-14: no critical or high finding, five medium and twelve low; all fixed except two low items, which are documented. The record is in the README under "Security audits".
